severityScale.critical: Can produce misleading evidence or unsafe state transition.
severityScale.high: Materially increases wrong-workflow or wrong-context risk.
severityScale.medium: Creates repeat friction or slows a meaningful user band.
severityScale.low: Polish or consistency issue without major workflow risk.

uxDebt.finding: Active Scenario and Version are not persistent in the global workspace context.
evidence: Header shows Project and compact cell/RF context.
Scenario/Version identity appears in Setup, Project menu, Run History, and Report detail.
uxDebt.impact: Users must reconstruct which saved inputs own a current result, a historical Run, or a Report.
uxDebt.nextAction: Concept 7G: add current/stale/historical lineage context around the existing shell.

uxDebt.finding: Setup, Propagation, RF Diagnostics, and Data mix multiple jobs in long drawers.
evidence: Propagation places common ray controls before path profile, Sub-THz, and P.1411 reference cards.
Data combines dataset, model, validation, and calibration.
uxDebt.impact: First-time and regular planners scan through research/reference detail before finding the next ordinary action.
uxDebt.nextAction: Introduce progressive disclosure and explicit Planning/Advanced/Research boundaries after lineage work.

uxDebt.finding: Inventory supports precise one-cell editing but not bulk planning.
evidence: First 250 matching cells are rendered.
Long list and editor share one drawer.
uxDebt.impact: Regular planners may need repeated single-cell edits and lose list context.
uxDebt.nextAction: Measure real bulk-edit tasks before selecting a safe bulk interaction model.

uxDebt.finding: Some empty states name a next action well; others describe future detail when no item can be selected.
evidence: Run History says select a Run when empty.
Report and Version empty states are more actionable but use storage-oriented copy.
uxDebt.impact: New users receive inconsistent guidance at the same lifecycle boundary.
uxDebt.nextAction: Standardize empty-state pattern: what exists, why empty, one next action.

uxDebt.finding: Map toolbar and layer menu are too dense at 1024px and 640px.
evidence: 1024px screenshot showed right-edge crowding/clipping.
640px DOM geometry placed the layer menu beyond the viewport.
uxDebt.impact: Focused map inspection remains possible, but full planning controls are unreliable on narrow layouts.
uxDebt.nextAction: Run a focused shell-quality pass with width-specific toolbar and layer-menu rules.

architectureDebt.finding: App.jsx is a large stateful orchestrator for shell, RF, optimization, Scenario, Run, Report, map, and diagnostics.
evidence: App.jsx is 5267 lines in the audited tree.
All major panels and many domain operations are imported and coordinated there.
architectureDebt.impact: IA changes can accidentally cross compute, persistence, and presentation boundaries; safe feature isolation is harder.
architectureDebt.nextAction: Use product-boundary adapters or route-level composition only when a concrete workflow phase needs it.

architectureDebt.finding: Stage, tool, result view, layer, Scenario, Version, and Run context are not URL-addressable.
evidence: The app renders a single shell at /.
No client-side route router was found.
architectureDebt.impact: Refresh, deep links, browser back, and shareable review context are weak.
architectureDebt.nextAction: Evaluate URL state only after lineage vocabulary is stable; do not introduce a router as a reflex.

architectureDebt.finding: Project menu, ScenarioPanel, Run History, Report artifacts, and revision inspector each own part of navigation.
evidence: Save Version and source/open actions have multiple entry points.
architectureDebt.impact: Valid workflows feel fragmented and target scope is harder to infer.
architectureDebt.nextAction: Define one lineage contract for labels, source summaries, and context actions.

performanceDebt.finding: Production JS is emitted as one 921.62 kB raw / 252.89 kB gzip main chunk.
evidence: Vite emitted the >500 kB warning.
App.jsx statically imports rare research, validation, Core Lab, experiment, and report tooling.
performanceDebt.impact: Initial load pays for features most users do not need on first interaction.
performanceDebt.nextAction: Generate a treemap and safely lazy-load product-boundary modules.

performanceDebt.finding: 451 cells, 161,784 building footprints, Leaflet layers, and optional result overlays share the map workspace.
evidence: Runtime logs and Data panel expose dataset scale.
MapCanvas renders multiple spatial layer types.
performanceDebt.impact: Map load, dataset switches, and layer toggles may feel heavier than control-panel actions.
performanceDebt.nextAction: Profile map interaction and layer toggles using representative Ankara data before optimizing.

accessibilityDebt.finding: The tool drawer is a modeless native dialog-shaped surface without evident focus containment or return behavior.
evidence: WorkspaceChrome renders a dialog with open and aria-modal=false.
Heading receives a ref/tabIndex, but an end-to-end focus contract was not evident.
accessibilityDebt.impact: Keyboard and assistive-technology users may lose context when the drawer changes.
accessibilityDebt.nextAction: Test and document focus entry, escape, outside interaction, and return-to-trigger behavior for drawer and project menu.

accessibilityDebt.finding: Spatial evidence is primarily visual; there is no complete keyboard-equivalent inventory of map features and layers.
evidence: Map markers/layers are rendered spatially; feature inspector opens through map interaction.
accessibilityDebt.impact: Non-pointer users cannot inspect the same evidence path with equal confidence.
accessibilityDebt.nextAction: Provide a synchronized selected-feature list or results table where the map is the primary visual.

accessibilityDebt.finding: Rail attention badges and icon-first controls can make state interpretation depend on symbol/color context.
evidence: Analyze rail shows ! in some states.
Map controls rely heavily on icons with tooltip/aria labels.
accessibilityDebt.impact: Unavailable, stale, or diagnostic states may be less discoverable without sight or prior knowledge.
accessibilityDebt.nextAction: Pair badges with text and preserve visible grouped labels at responsive widths.

terminologyDebt.finding: Current, historical, and stale are not one shared user-facing vocabulary.
evidence: Plan changed is used for invalidation.
Historical/source language appears in Run/Report detail.
Current result is implied by Results.
terminologyDebt.impact: Users can understand individual screens but not always the relationship among states.
terminologyDebt.nextAction: Adopt explicit state labels and source summaries in Concept 7G.

terminologyDebt.finding: Retained report artifact, generator, hash, and evidence status appear in ordinary Report flow.
evidence: ReportArtifactsPanel is nested in ReportExportPanel.
Visible copy includes retained artifacts and artifact counts.
terminologyDebt.impact: Report creation feels like storage management for non-reviewer users.
terminologyDebt.nextAction: Lead with Report/Download/source; keep artifact metadata behind detail.

terminologyDebt.finding: Cell, tower, and site describe different levels but are not always explicitly scoped.
evidence: Inventory and Run contexts use cell; Report copy uses selected tower.
terminologyDebt.impact: Users may infer that a physical tower and RF cell are the same entity.
terminologyDebt.nextAction: Use cell in RF scope and site/tower only for physical placement context.

prioritySummary.reason: It directly reduces the two critical risks using existing domain and persistence concepts before larger disclosure, responsive, or performance work.

invariance: This register records debt only; it does not authorize or implement fixes.
